solutionSteps: \textnormal{Let }S_M\textnormal{ denote the first M terms of the unweighted alternating logarithmic series. Pairing terms and using the Gamma recurrence gives a finite identity.}
\textnormal{The adjacent odd partial sum includes one additional positive logarithm. Averaging the neighboring even and odd partial sums cancels their growing logarithms.}
\textnormal{Therefore the averages of all partial sums tend to this same value. A second summation-by-parts identity turns those Cesaro averages into the requested Abel limit.}

\textnormal{The nonnegative weights on the right sum to one, and every fixed initial segment has total weight tending to zero. Since the Cesaro averages converge, their weighted average has the same limit.}
